title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page (p. 111 of Exposé IX), not a manuscript note. It belongs to SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §9.4. It looks misfiled among the handwritten notes on graded comodules over a coalgebra S and the dual S^k-modules (previous and next pages).

Setting: S is the spectrum of a (strictly) henselian discrete valuation ring R with generic point η. Q and P are Néron models, presumably those of an abelian variety and its dual. H is a finite étale group scheme (in the application, the group of connected components), with special fibre H_o. D(H) = Hom(H, G_m) is its Cartier dual, and Ȟ_o = Hom(H_o, Q/Z).

What the page does: it supplies the isomorphism d) left over from 9.4.3. Over an arbitrary base U it constructs a natural map
  G_m(U) ⊗ Ȟ_o → H^1(U, D(H_oU)).
Take m ≥ 1 with mH_o = 0. Then D(H_o) ≅ μ_m ⊗ Ȟ_o (with Ȟ_o = Hom(H_o, Z/m)). The map is the composite of three arrows:
- the Kummer coboundary ∂ : G_m(U) → H^1(U, μ_m), tensored with Ȟ_o;
- the cup-product-type arrow H^1(U, μ_m) ⊗ Ȟ_o → H^1(U, μ_m ⊗ Ȟ_o);
- the identification b), μ_m ⊗ Ȟ_o ≅ D(H_o).

The page then claims:
- the map is independent of the choice of m (left to the reader);
- it is always injective;
- its cokernel is Hom(H_o, Pic U), hence zero when Pic(U) = 0.
Proof: reduce to H_o = Z/n. There the Kummer sequence 0 → G_m(U)/n → H^1(U, μ_n) → Pic(U)[n] → 0 gives the result directly.

Corollary 9.4.4. Apply this with U = η (Pic = 0) and U = S, using G_m(η)/G_m(S) = K*/R* ≅ Z (via the valuation). This gives
  H^1(η, D(H)_η) / Im H^1(S, D(H)) ≅ Z ⊗ Ȟ_o = Ȟ_o.
Combined with a) and b), the obstruction group to extending extensions of Q_η by P_η over S becomes
  Ext^1(Q_η, P_η) / Im Ext^1(Q, P) ≅ Q̌_o ⊗ Q̌*_o,
the tensor product of the duals of the two component groups. This step is part of Grothendieck's construction of the pairing on component groups that is now called Grothendieck's pairing.
errors: 'm ≥ 0' should read m ≥ 1 (m > 0), since m must kill H_o and μ_0 makes no sense here.
In the composite, the middle term is typed 'Ȟ^o' instead of Ȟ_o, and the target D(H_oS) should be D(H_oU).
Formula e) is missing the closing parenthesis in Im H^1(S, D(H)).
Minor gaps: independence of m, and the passage from G_m(η)/G_m(S) ≅ Z to e), are left to the reader. Both are routine and correct.

ideas.what: Kummer-coboundary map G_m(U) ⊗ Ȟ_o → H^1(U, D(H_o)): injective with cokernel Hom(H_o, Pic U).
ideas.modern_name: Kummer theory for Cartier duals of finite constant groups.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Kummer theory); written in this form by Grothendieck in SGA 7.

ideas.what: Computing the obstruction group Ext^1(Q_η, P_η)/Im Ext^1(Q, P) as the tensor product of the duals of the component groups.
ideas.modern_name: Groundwork for Grothendieck's pairing on Néron component groups.

missed.claim: Archival point only: this typed SGA 7 IX page (stamped 429) sits in cote 136, the divided-power De Rham notes, between handwritten pages on graded comodules. It looks misfiled or reused as scrap paper. There is no new mathematics; the content is published in SGA 7.
missed.quote: Corollaire 9.4.4. Avec les notations de 9.4.3 on a un isomorphisme canonique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relevant only to cataloguing the archive and dating the typescripts.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX, §9.4. Its content is fully in the literature and credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: 'H^1(U,μ_m) ⊗ Ȟ^o' should be 'H^1(U,μ_m) ⊗ Ȟ_o' (the typescript itself has the superscript typo).
Final term of the composite reads H^1(U, D(H_oS)) in the typescript; the intended object is D(H_oU).
'{+c+}anonique' is the typescript word 'canonique' with a handwritten caret mark near it; it is not an insertion.
The bottom has a stamped archive number 429 and a faint handwritten 157 (archive page) in the margin.
